sanskrit: guṇavanty annapānāni bhojyāni vividhāni ca mālyāni ca sugandhīni tāni rājā dadau tataḥ
english: Wholesome food and drink of many kinds, diverse delicacies, and fragrant garlands — all these the king then bestowed.

sanskrit: viśeṣataś ca vāsārthaṃ sabhāṃ grāme vṛkasthale vidadhe kauravo rājā bahuratnāṃ manoramām
english: And in particular, for a residence, the Kaurava king arranged a charming assembly hall adorned with many jewels in the village of Vṛkasthala.

sanskrit: etad vidhāya vai sarvaṃ devārham atimānuṣam ācakhyau dhṛtarāṣṭrāya rājā duryodhanas tadā
english: Having made all these arrangements — worthy of the gods and beyond human — King Duryodhana then reported them to Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tāḥ sabhāḥ keśavaḥ sarvā ratnāni vividhāni ca asamīkṣyaiva dāśārha upāyāt kurusadma tat
english: Without even inspecting those assembly halls or the various jewels, Keśava of the Dāśārha line made his way to the Kuru palace.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca upaplavyād iha kṣattar upayāto janārdanaḥ vṛkasthale nivasati sa ca prātar iheṣyati
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Kṣattṛ, Janārdana has arrived here from Upaplavya; he is staying at Vṛkasthala and will come here tomorrow morning.

sanskrit: āhukānām adhipatiḥ purogaḥ sarvasātvatām mahāmanā mahāvīryo mahāmātro janārdanaḥ
english: Janārdana, lord of the Āhukas, foremost among all the Sātvatas, great of soul, great of valor, and great of measure —

sanskrit: sphītasya vṛṣṇivaṃśasya bhartā goptā ca mādhavaḥ trayāṇām api lokānāṃ bhagavān prapitāmahaḥ
english: Mādhava, the sustainer and protector of the prosperous Vṛṣṇi lineage, the blessed lord who is the great forefather of all three worlds —

sanskrit: vṛṣṇyandhakāḥ sumanaso yasya prajñām upāsate ādityā vasavo rudrā yathā buddhiṃ bṛhaspateḥ
english: The Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas of glad heart revere his wisdom as the Ādityas, Vasus, and Rudras revere the intellect of Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: tasmai pūjāṃ prayokṣyāmi dāśārhāya mahātmane pratyakṣaṃ tava dharmajña tan me kathayataḥ śṛṇu
english: I shall bestow worship upon that great-souled one of the Dāśārha line. O knower of dharma, hear me as I describe it before you.

sanskrit: ekavarṇaiḥ sukṛṣṇāṅgair bāhlijātair hayottamaiḥ caturyuktān rathāṃs tasmai raukmān dāsyāmi ṣoḍaśa
english: I will give him sixteen golden chariots, each yoked with four of the finest horses of Bāhlika breed, uniform in color with beautiful dark limbs.

sanskrit: nityaprabhinnān mātaṅgān īṣādantān prahāriṇaḥ aṣṭānucaram ekaikam aṣṭau dāsyāmi keśave
english: I will give Keśava eight elephants, perpetually in rut, with tusks like poles, fierce strikers, each accompanied by eight attendants.

sanskrit: dāsīnām aprajātānāṃ śubhānāṃ rukmavarcasām śatam asmai pradāsyāmi dāsānām api tāvataḥ
english: I will give him a hundred fair maidservants who have not borne children, glowing like gold, and as many male servants likewise.

sanskrit: āvikaṃ bahu susparśaṃ pārvatīyair upāhṛtam tad apy asmai pradāsyāmi sahasrāṇi daśāṣṭa ca
english: I will give him eighteen thousand woolen cloths, soft to the touch, brought from the mountain folk.

sanskrit: ajinānāṃ sahasrāṇi cīnadeśodbhavāni ca tāny apy asmai pradāsyāmi yāvad arhati keśavaḥ
english: Thousands of hides from the land of China — these too I will give him, as many as Keśava deserves.

sanskrit: divā rātrau ca bhāty eṣa sutejā vimalo maṇiḥ tam apy asmai pradāsyāmi tam apy arhati keśavaḥ
english: This gem, blazing with great radiance, pure and shining by day and night alike — that too I will give him, for Keśava deserves it too.

sanskrit: ekenāpi pataty ahnā yojanāni caturdaśa yānam aśvatarīyuktaṃ dāsye tasmai tad apy aham
english: And I will give him a conveyance yoked with mules that can cover fourteen yojanas in a single day.

sanskrit: yāvanti vāhanāny asya yāvantaḥ puruṣāś ca te tato 'ṣṭaguṇam apy asmai bhojyaṃ dāsyāmy ahaṃ sadā
english: Whatever vehicles he has and however many men accompany him, I will always provide him provisions eight times that number.

sanskrit: mama putrāś ca pautrāś ca sarve duryodhanād ṛte pratyudyāsyanti dāśārhaṃ rathair mṛṣṭair alaṃkṛtāḥ
english: All my sons and grandsons — all except Duryodhana — will go forth to receive the Dāśārha hero, adorned and mounted on gleaming chariots.

sanskrit: svalaṃkṛtāś ca kalyāṇyaḥ pādair eva sahasraśaḥ vāramukhyā mahābhāgaṃ pratyudyāsyanti keśavam
english: And auspicious women of the foremost courtesans, finely adorned, will go forth on foot by the thousands to receive the illustrious Keśava.

sanskrit: nagarād api yāḥ kāś cid gamiṣyanti janārdanam draṣṭuṃ kanyāś ca kalyāṇyas tāś ca yāsyanty anāvṛtāḥ
english: And whatever auspicious maidens from the city may go to see Janārdana — they too shall go forth unveiled.

sanskrit: sastrīpuruṣabālaṃ hi nagaraṃ madhusūdanam udīkṣate mahātmānaṃ bhānumantam iva prajāḥ
english: Indeed, the city — men, women, and children together — gazes upon the great-souled Madhusūdana as the people gaze upon the sun.

sanskrit: mahādhvajapatākāś ca kriyantāṃ sarvatodiśam jalāvasikto virajāḥ panthās tasyeti cānvaśāt
english: Let great banners and flags be raised in all directions, and let the road be sprinkled with water and made spotless — so he commanded.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanasya ca gṛhaṃ duryodhanagṛhād varam tad asya kriyatāṃ kṣipraṃ susaṃmṛṣṭam alaṃkṛtam
english: And the house of Duḥśāsana, finer than Duryodhana's own — let it be quickly swept clean and adorned for him.

sanskrit: etad dhi rucirākāraiḥ prāsādair upaśobhitam śivaṃ ca ramaṇīyaṃ ca sarvartu sumahādhanam
english: For it is graced with beautiful palaces of pleasing appearance, auspicious and delightful, well-appointed with great wealth in every season.

sanskrit: sarvam asmin gṛhe ratnaṃ mama duryodhanasya ca yad yad arhet sa vārṣṇeyas tat tad deyam asaṃśayam
english: Whatever jewel or treasure in this house — mine or Duryodhana's — that hero of the Vṛṣṇis may deserve, that without doubt must be given.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca rājan bahumataś cāsi trailokyasyāpi sattamaḥ saṃbhāvitaś ca lokasya saṃmataś cāsi bhārata
english: Vidura said: O king, you are held in high esteem as the best among people even in all three worlds; you are honored and respected by the world, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yat tvam evaṃgate brūyāḥ paścime vayasi sthitaḥ śāstrād vā supratarkād vā susthiraḥ sthaviro hy asi
english: That you, standing in the last stage of life, should speak thus — whether from scripture or sound reasoning — is fitting, for you are a steadfast elder.

sanskrit: lekhāśmanīva bhāḥ sūrye mahormir iva sāgare dharmas tvayi mahān rājann iti vyavasitāḥ prajāḥ
english: As sunlight upon a touchstone, as a great wave upon the ocean — so great is the dharma in you, O king: thus the people are convinced.

sanskrit: sadaiva bhāvito loko guṇaughais tava pārthiva guṇānāṃ rakṣaṇe nityaṃ prayatasva sabāndhavaḥ
english: The world has ever been nourished by the flood of your virtues, O king; strive always to protect those virtues, together with your kinsmen.

sanskrit: ārjavaṃ pratipadyasva mā bālyād bahudhā naśīḥ rājyaṃ putrāṃś ca pautrāṃś ca suhṛdaś cāpi supriyān
english: Embrace uprightness; do not lose in many ways through childishness — your kingdom, your sons and grandsons, and your dearest friends.

sanskrit: yat tvaṃ ditsasi kṛṣṇāya rājann atithaye bahu etad anyac ca dāśārhaḥ pṛthivīm api cārhati
english: What you wish to give Kṛṣṇa as a guest is much, and more besides — the Dāśārha hero deserves the very earth itself.

sanskrit: na tu tvaṃ dharmam uddiśya tasya vā priyakāraṇāt etad icchasi kṛṣṇāya satyenātmānam ālabhe
english: Yet it is not for dharma's sake nor out of love for him that you desire to do this for Kṛṣṇa — I swear this by my own self in truth.

sanskrit: māyaiṣātattvam evaitac chadmaitad bhūridakṣiṇa jānāmi te mataṃ rājan gūḍhaṃ bāhyena karmaṇā
english: This is illusion, not reality; this is deceit, O giver of great gifts. I know your hidden intention, O king, concealed beneath this outward act.

sanskrit: pañca pañcaiva lipsanti grāmakān pāṇḍavā nṛpa na ca ditsasi tebhyas tāṃs tac chamaṃ kaḥ kariṣyati
english: The Pāṇḍavas seek just five villages, O king, and you will not give even those to them — who then will bring about peace?

sanskrit: arthena tu mahābāhuṃ vārṣṇeyaṃ tvaṃ jihīrṣasi anenaivābhyupāyena pāṇḍavebhyo bibhitsasi
english: By wealth you wish to win over the mighty-armed Vārṣṇeya, and by this very stratagem you seek to separate him from the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: na ca vittena śakyo 'sau nodyamena na garhayā anyo dhanaṃjayāt kartum etat tattvaṃ bravīmi te
english: He cannot be won over by wealth, nor by effort, nor by reproach — no one other than Dhanañjaya can accomplish this. I speak this truth to you.

sanskrit: veda kṛṣṇasya māhātmyaṃ vedāsya dṛḍhabhaktitām atyājyam asya jānāmi prāṇais tulyaṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: He knows Kṛṣṇa's greatness; he knows Kṛṣṇa's steadfast devotion. I know that Dhanañjaya is inseparable from him — equal to his own life.

sanskrit: anyat kumbhād apāṃ pūrṇād anyat pādāvasecanāt anyat kuśalasaṃpraśnān naiṣiṣyati janārdanaḥ
english: Beyond a pot filled with water, the washing of his feet, and courteous inquiry after his well-being, Janārdana will accept nothing more.

sanskrit: yat tv asya priyam ātithyaṃ mānārhasya mahātmanaḥ tad asmai kriyatāṃ rājan mānārho hi janārdanaḥ
english: Whatever hospitality is dear to that great-souled one who is worthy of honor — let that be rendered to him, O king, for Janārdana is worthy of honor.

sanskrit: āśaṃsamānaḥ kalyāṇaṃ kurūn abhyeti keśavaḥ yenaiva rājann arthena tad evāsmā upākuru
english: Keśava comes to the Kurus hoping for an auspicious outcome; for that very purpose he comes, O king — serve him accordingly.

sanskrit: śamam icchati dāśārhas tava duryodhanasya ca pāṇḍavānāṃ ca rājendra tad asya vacanaṃ kuru
english: The Dāśārha hero desires peace — between you, Duryodhana, and the Pāṇḍavas, O lord of kings. Do as he says.

sanskrit: pitāsi rājan putrās te vṛddhas tvaṃ śiśavaḥ pare vartasva pitṛvat teṣu vartante te hi putravat
english: You are their father, O king; your sons are grown but the others are as children. Act toward them as a father, for they act toward you as sons.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca yad āha viduraḥ kṛṣṇe sarvaṃ tat satyam ucyate anurakto hy asaṃhāryaḥ pārthān prati janārdanaḥ
english: Duryodhana said: What Vidura says about Kṛṣṇa is all truly spoken — Janārdana is devoted to the Pārthas and cannot be swayed.

sanskrit: yat tu satkārasaṃyuktaṃ deyaṃ vasu janārdane anekarūpaṃ rājendra na tad deyaṃ kadā cana
english: But the manifold wealth and honor that would be given to Janārdana as tribute — that, O lord of kings, must never be given.

sanskrit: deśaḥ kālas tathāyukto na hi nārhati keśavaḥ maṃsyaty adhokṣajo rājan bhayād arcati mām iti
english: The place, the time, the occasion — Keśava is no doubt deserving. But, O king, Adhokṣaja will think: 'He honors me out of fear.'

sanskrit: avamānaś ca yatra syāt kṣatriyasya viśāṃ pate na tat kuryād budhaḥ kāryam iti me niścitā matiḥ
english: And where there is humiliation for a Kṣatriya, O lord of the people, a wise man should not do such a deed — this is my firm conviction.

sanskrit: sa hi pūjyatamo devaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ kamalalocanaḥ trayāṇām api lokānāṃ viditaṃ mama sarvathā
english: For Kṛṣṇa the lotus-eyed is the most adorable of gods throughout all three worlds — this I know fully and in every way.

sanskrit: na tu tasmin pradeyaṃ syāt tathā kāryagatiḥ prabho vigrahaḥ samupārabdho na hi śāmyaty avigrahāt
english: But according to the course of affairs, nothing should be given to him now, O lord. War once begun does not subside except through war.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā bhīṣmaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ vaicitravīryaṃ rājānam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing those words of his, Bhīṣma the grandsire of the Kurus spoke these words to King Vaicitravīrya.

sanskrit: satkṛto 'satkṛto vāpi na krudhyeta janārdanaḥ nālam anyam avajñātum avajñāto 'pi keśavaḥ
english: Whether honored or dishonored, Janārdana would not grow angry; even when slighted, Keśava is not one to slight another in return.

sanskrit: yat tu kāryaṃ mahābāho manasā kāryatāṃ gatam sarvopāyair na tac chakyaṃ kena cit kartum anyathā
english: But what purpose has been determined in his mind as to be accomplished, O mighty-armed one, cannot by any means be altered by anyone.

sanskrit: sa yad brūyān mahābāhus tat kāryam aviśaṅkayā vāsudevena tīrthena kṣipraṃ saṃśāmya pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: Whatever the mighty-armed one says should be done without hesitation; make peace with the Pāṇḍavas quickly through Vāsudeva as the sacred ford.

sanskrit: dharmyam arthyaṃ sa dharmātmā dhruvaṃ vaktā janārdanaḥ tasmin vācyāḥ priyā vāco bhavatā bāndhavaiḥ saha
english: That dharma-souled Janārdana will surely speak what is just and beneficial; to him must you and your kinsmen speak pleasing words.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca na paryāyo 'sti yad rājañ śriyaṃ niṣkevalām aham taiḥ sahemām upāśnīyāṃ jīvañ jīvaiḥ pitāmaha
english: Duryodhana said: There is no alternative, O king, that I, while living among the living, O grandsire, should enjoy this sovereignty in full together with them.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu sumahat kāryaṃ śṛṇu me yat samarthitam parāyaṇaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ niyaṃsyāmi janārdanam
english: But hear this great plan I have devised: I will bind Janārdana, the mainstay of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tasmin baddhe bhaviṣyanti vṛṣṇayaḥ pṛthivī tathā pāṇḍavāś ca vidheyā me sa ca prātar iheṣyati
english: With him bound, the Vṛṣṇis, the earth, and the Pāṇḍavas will all be subject to me — and he is coming here tomorrow morning.

sanskrit: atropāyaṃ yathā samyaṅ na budhyeta janārdanaḥ na cāpāyo bhavet kaś cit tad bhavān prabravītu me
english: Here, tell me the means by which Janārdana shall not perceive the plan in time, and whereby no harm may befall us.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā ghoraṃ kṛṣṇābhisaṃhitam dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ sahāmātyo vyathito vimanābhavat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing those terrible words aimed against Kṛṣṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra together with his ministers was tormented and became despondent.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanam idaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bravīd vacaḥ maivaṃ vocaḥ prajāpāla naiṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Then Dhṛtarāṣṭra spoke these words to Duryodhana: Do not speak thus, O protector of the people — this is not eternal dharma.

sanskrit: dūtaś ca hi hṛṣīkeśaḥ saṃbandhī ca priyaś ca naḥ apāpaḥ kauraveyeṣu kathaṃ bandhanam arhati
english: For Hṛṣīkeśa comes as an envoy, is our kinsman, and is dear to us; he is blameless among the Kauravas — how could he deserve imprisonment?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca parīto dhṛtarāṣṭrāyaṃ tava putraḥ sumandadhīḥ vṛṇoty anarthaṃ na tv arthaṃ yācyamānaḥ suhṛdgaṇaiḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: O Dhṛtarāṣṭra, surrounded by your counselors, this dim-witted son of yours chooses calamity and not benefit, even when implored by his friends.

sanskrit: imam utpathi vartantaṃ pāpaṃ pāpānubandhinam vākyāni suhṛdāṃ hitvā tvam apy asyānuvartase
english: This one walks a crooked path, sinful and attended by sin, and having abandoned the counsel of friends — and you too follow along after him.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇam akliṣṭakarmāṇam āsādyāyaṃ sudurmatiḥ tava putraḥ sahāmātyaḥ kṣaṇena na bhaviṣyati
english: Having dared to lay hands on Kṛṣṇa whose deeds are without effort, this utterly wicked son of yours together with his ministers will cease to exist in a moment.

sanskrit: pāpasyāsya nṛśaṃsasya tyaktadharmasya durmateḥ notsahe 'narthasaṃyuktāṃ vācaṃ śrotuṃ kathaṃ cana
english: I cannot in any way bear to listen to words full of such ruinous intent from this sinful, cruel, dharma-forsaking, evil-minded one.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā bharataśreṣṭho vṛddhaḥ paramamanyumān utthāya tasmāt prātiṣṭhad bhīṣmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, Bhīṣma, best of the Bhāratas, old but filled with great fury, rose from his seat and departed, he whose valor is in truth.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca prātar utthāya kṛṣṇas tu kṛtavān sarvam āhnikam brāhmaṇair abhyanujñātaḥ prayayau nagaraṃ prati
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Rising early in the morning, Kṛṣṇa performed all his daily rites; then, blessed by the Brāhmaṇas, he set out toward the city.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntaṃ mahābāhum anujñāpya tato nṛpa paryavartanta te sarve vṛkasthalanivāsinaḥ
english: Having bid farewell to that mighty-armed one as he departed, O king, all the residents of Vṛkasthala turned back.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrās tam āyāntaṃ pratyujjagmuḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ duryodhanam ṛte sarve bhīṣmadroṇakṛpādayaḥ
english: The Dhārtarāṣṭras went forth adorned to receive him as he came — all of them except Duryodhana: Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, and the rest.

sanskrit: paurāś ca bahulā rājan hṛṣīkeśaṃ didṛkṣavaḥ yānair bahuvidhair anye padbhir eva tathāpare
english: And many citizens, O king, eager to see Hṛṣīkeśa, came out — some in various kinds of vehicles, and others simply on foot.

sanskrit: sa vai pathi samāgamya bhīṣmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā droṇena dhārtarāṣṭraiś ca tair vṛto nagaraṃ yayau
english: Meeting on the road with Bhīṣma of effortless deeds, with Droṇa, and with those Dhārtarāṣṭras, he proceeded to the city, surrounded by them all.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇasaṃmānanārthaṃ ca nagaraṃ samalaṃkṛtam babhūvū rājamārgāś ca bahuratnasamācitāḥ
english: For the sake of honoring Kṛṣṇa, the city was beautifully adorned and the royal roads were strewn with many jewels.

sanskrit: na sma kaś cid gṛhe rājaṃs tad āsīd bharatarṣabha na strī na vṛddho na śiśur vāsudevadidṛkṣayā
english: Not a single person remained at home, O king, O bull of the Bhāratas — no woman, no elder, no child — all out of eagerness to see Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: rājamārge narā na sma saṃbhavanty avaniṃ gatāḥ tathā hi sumahad rājan hṛṣīkeśapraveśane
english: The men on the royal road could scarcely touch the ground, so great, O king, was the press at the entry of Hṛṣīkeśa.

sanskrit: āvṛtāni varastrībhir gṛhāṇi sumahānty api pracalantīva bhāreṇa dṛśyante sma mahītale
english: Even the great houses, thronged by the finest women who crowded their rooftops, appeared as if trembling under the weight, as seen from the earth.

sanskrit: tathā ca gatimantas te vāsudevasya vājinaḥ pranaṣṭagatayo 'bhūvan rājamārge narair vṛte
english: And the swift horses of Vāsudeva lost all their swiftness, the royal road being so packed with people.

sanskrit: sa gṛhaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya prāviśac chatrukarśanaḥ pāṇḍuraṃ puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ prāsādair upaśobhitam
english: The lotus-eyed one, crusher of foes, entered the white palace of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, beautified with its many halls.

sanskrit: tisraḥ kakṣyā vyatikramya keśavo rājaveśmanaḥ vaicitravīryaṃ rājānam abhyagacchad ariṃdamaḥ
english: Passing through three courtyards of the royal dwelling, Keśava the subduer of enemies approached King Vaicitravīrya.

sanskrit: abhyāgacchati dāśārhe prajñācakṣur nareśvaraḥ sahaiva droṇabhīṣmābhyām udatiṣṭhan mahāyaśāḥ
english: As the Dāśārha hero approached, the king who sees with wisdom's eye, that lord of men of great renown, rose along with Droṇa and Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: kṛpaś ca somadattaś ca mahārājaś ca bāhlikaḥ āsanebhyo 'calan sarve pūjayanto janārdanam
english: Kṛpa, Somadatta, and the great king Bāhlika — all rose from their seats in honor of Janārdana.

sanskrit: tato rājānam āsādya dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ yaśasvinam sa bhīṣmaṃ pūjayām āsa vārṣṇeyo vāgbhir añjasā
english: Then, having approached the illustrious king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Vārṣṇeya paid homage to Bhīṣma with fitting words.
